claim_text: Valcour's vendor told the state late on Nov 16 of a potential security incident
summary: The state says CrossWind Technologies, which operates Valcour, notified it late on Monday, Nov 16, of a potential security incident.
detail: The state's own statements say 'potential security incident'. The vendor has published no statement that we found; we have its notice only through the state.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 17 state statement gives the date and the vendor's notice; WCAX reports the same.

claim_text: The state helped take Valcour offline as a precaution and cut off connected state systems
summary: The state says that once notified it helped the vendor take Valcour offline 'as a precaution' and 'contained all state systems that connect to it'.
detail: The statement does not give the time the system went down.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 17 state statement says both in its own words.

claim_text: Valcour went offline either late Monday night or on Tuesday, Nov 17; reports differ
summary: VTDigger first reported Valcour went offline Monday night; WCAX, WPTZ and a later VTDigger story say Tuesday, the later one Tuesday morning.
detail: The state's statements give no time. We use Nov 17 as the offline date and treat the exact time as unsettled.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Three outlets give the offline time; they disagree, so only the range is reported.

claim_text: Valcour runs dispatch and records for nearly all Vermont police and many fire and EMS agencies
summary: The state says Valcour handles dispatch and records for nearly all law enforcement and supports many fire and EMS operations in Vermont.
detail: It tracks incidents from the first call to the end of a case and is the central store for reports. Agencies share its data.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 18 state statement describes the system in these words.

claim_text: Valcour serves 35 police and 62 fire and EMS agencies
summary: WCAX reports that Valcour handles dispatch and police records for 35 police and 62 fire and EMS agencies across Vermont.
detail: The state has not published these counts in the statements we read. One outlet gives them.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: WCAX states both numbers.

claim_text: 911 and emergency response are not affected
summary: The state says 911 and emergency responses are unaffected, and non-emergency department phone lines work as normal.
detail: Repeated in the Nov 17, 18 and 20 statements.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: All three state statements say so directly.

claim_text: Agencies have moved to backup procedures: paper, radio and phone
summary: The state says agencies moved to backup procedures. Reporters describe cases filed on paper and information passed by radio and phone.
detail: A county sheriff told the Boston Globe dispatchers are writing calls on paper and sending them by radio and phone. The state says some records work is slower.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The state confirms backup procedures; WCAX and the Boston Globe independently describe paper and radio.

claim_text: State criminal history and national crime databases are still available to police
summary: The state says other key criminal justice systems, including state criminal history records and national crime information databases, remain available.
detail: This is separate from the FBI crime database story reported on Nov 20; the state was speaking about police access, not that story.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 17 and Nov 18 state statements say so directly.

claim_text: Valcour will stay offline until the investigation ends and weaknesses are fixed; there is no timeline
summary: The state says Valcour cannot come back online until the investigation is complete, and on Nov 24 it said it still has no timeline for restoring it.
detail: The Nov 20 statement said it stays down until the investigation is done and any identified vulnerabilities are fixed. The Nov 24 statement from the Public Safety commissioner says the investigations by state officials, federal partners and the vendor are still active and the system cannot return until that work is complete.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 24 and Nov 20 state statements say both in their own words.

claim_text: The state calls it a 'security incident' whose nature and scope are still being determined
summary: State statements describe 'the security incident affecting the use of Valcour' and, on Nov 24, 'the security incident that prompted the outage', and say its nature and scope are still being investigated.
detail: Officials have not used the words breach, intrusion, ransomware or cyberattack in the statements we read, including the Nov 24 statement.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The words come from the state statements themselves.

claim_text: Valcour was breached or hit by a cyberattack
summary: Some coverage calls it a breach, but officials have not said an attacker got in. The state's IT chief told VTDigger officials are not jumping to conclusions about whether it was a cyberattack.
detail: WCAX's headline says 'breach'; the state says 'potential security incident' and 'security incident'.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: VTDigger reports officials have not concluded it was a cyberattack; the state statements do not say so either.

claim_text: Who was behind it is not known
summary: WCAX reports there is no indication of who is responsible. No group has claimed it in any source we found.
detail: Absence of a claim is not proof there was no attacker.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: WCAX says there is no indication of who is responsible.

claim_text: Whether any police or personal data was accessed or taken is not known
summary: No statement or report says whether data was viewed, copied or changed.
detail: Valcour holds police reports and case records, so this is the main open question for the public.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The state says the nature and scope are still under investigation; the Globe says the incident was not described.

claim_text: The state has notified the Vermont Attorney General's Office and the FBI
summary: The Nov 20 state statement says the Department of Public Safety and Agency of Digital Services notified the Attorney General's Office and the FBI.
detail: The state says 'notified'. The FBI has since commented through a spokesperson; the Attorney General has not commented publicly in any source we found.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 20 state statement says so directly.

claim_text: The FBI and the Attorney General are investigating
summary: WCAX reports the FBI and the attorney general are now investigating. VTDigger reports the governor said Thursday the FBI is now involved.
detail: The FBI's Albany office told WPTZ on Nov 23 it is 'fully engaged' and assisting (see the FBI claim in this section). The Attorney General has not commented publicly in any source we found, and only WCAX says the Attorney General is investigating.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets report FBI involvement; only WCAX says the Attorney General is investigating.

claim_text: No cause has been published
summary: Neither the state nor the vendor has said what happened. On Nov 24 the state said it is still working with its partners 'to understand exactly what happened'.
detail: No root cause is published, so the case stays open. The Nov 24 statement mentions 'numerous incidents nationwide in recent weeks' only as a reason to prepare; it does not link them to Valcour.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The Nov 24 and Nov 20 statements give no cause; the Globe says the state did not describe the incident and the vendor declined interviews.

claim_text: Vermont's IT chief said there is no evidence it is related to other recent incidents
summary: The state's chief information officer told VTDigger on Nov 18: 'We haven't seen evidence that this event is related to other recent incidents.'
detail: Said to a reporter, not in a written statement. WCAX on Nov 19 said it is unknown whether it is related to the national outages.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: VTDigger quotes the official directly.

claim_text: Gov. Phil Scott said there are 'too many points of coincidence' and he is skeptical
summary: WPTZ quotes the governor: 'I'm not a conspiracy theorist, but there's just too many points of coincidence to make this a coincidence.' He said he looks forward to the full investigation.
detail: This is the governor's view, not a finding. It is not clear whether he meant Valcour or the week's outages in general.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: WPTZ quotes the governor directly.

claim_text: Vermont's Public Utility Commission website was also taken offline over suspicious activity
summary: VTDigger reports the Public Utility Commission website was taken offline due to suspicious activity.
detail: No source links it to Valcour. It is not covered on this page beyond this note.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: VTDigger reports it in passing.

claim_text: Valcour is operated by California-based CrossWind Technologies and was built with Burlington police
summary: The Boston Globe reports Valcour was developed about 15 years ago by Burlington police with CrossWind, and the state police moved to it in 2021.
detail: The state names CrossWind Technologies Inc. as the vendor; the history comes from the Globe, citing Seven Days.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Globe gives the history; the state statement names the vendor.

claim_text: The FBI says it is engaged and helping Vermont with the investigation
summary: An FBI Albany spokesperson told WPTZ: 'FBI Albany is fully engaged with our partners in Vermont and working to provide any resources necessary to assist.'
detail: This confirms FBI involvement, which WCAX and VTDigger also report. The FBI did not say what happened, whether there was an intrusion, or whether data was taken.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: WPTZ quotes the FBI's own statement; WCAX and VTDigger independently report FBI involvement.

claim_text: State police say the outage has had no negative impact on public safety
summary: The state police emergency communications director told WPTZ the backup operation is working and there is 'no negative impact on public safety'.
detail: Said to a reporter. A local dispatch supervisor told WPTZ staff are tracking notes on paper and that past records are not available to them. The director said he has not seen an outage of this kind last this long.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: WPTZ quotes the state police official directly.

claim_text: The state is looking at other dispatch systems to replace manual data entry
summary: The Public Safety commissioner says the department is evaluating alternative computer-aided-dispatch systems that agencies could use instead of the manual data entry dispatchers have done since Valcour went offline.
detail: The state has not named any system or said when one might be used. It says it will share details with agencies and the public.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 24 state statement says so in its own words.

claim_text: The biggest public-facing effect is on public records requests and other administrative work
summary: The state says the most significant impact on the public is on the public records request process and other administrative services that need Valcour, and asks people with pending requests for patience.
detail: The state says police, fire and EMS service continues and 911 and phone lines are unaffected.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Nov 24 state statement says so directly.
